prompt.context: Your client is the CEO of Cup Co, a national supplier of Styrofoam cups to restaurants. While profit has been steady, she is worried about the influx of cheaper products from China by a new competitor (Chalice Inc) and has called you in to give a recommendation on how to ensure continued profitability.
prompt.question: How should Cup Co ensure continued profitability in the face of cheaper competition from Chalice Inc?

clarifying_info.a: Cup Co's customer base consists only of restaurant chains in the US (think McDonald's etc.)

clarifying_info.q: How many products does Cup Co sell?
clarifying_info.a: For the purpose of this case, assume Cup Co has only one product
Cup Co manufactures its product in the US

clarifying_info.q: What do we know about Chalice Inc?
clarifying_info.a: Chalice Inc is a Chinese-based company with no other product in the US

exhibits.title: Cost and Price Structure
exhibits.shows: A table comparing per-unit economics (in cents) for Cup Co and Chalice Inc across price, manufacturing cost, shipping cost, and distribution cost

exhibits.title: Customer Preferences and Competitor Scores
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of customers who rank service reliability, price, and design as their top preference; and two score charts (0-10) comparing Cup Co and Chalice Inc on design and service reliability

framework: Frame analysis relative to Cup Co vs. Chalice Inc (comparison table approach)
Financial considerations: profitability tree — Revenue (customers, units sold, price per unit) vs. Cost (fixed manufacturing, variable manufacturing, shipping, distribution overhead)
Non-financial considerations: Customer preferences and what matters to them
Non-financial considerations: Competitive landscape — both new entrant (Chalice Inc) and existing competitors

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the profitability (margin per unit) for both Cup Co and Chalice Inc. What does this tell you?
questions.guidance: Strong answer: Cup Co profit = 10 - 4 - 3 = 3 cents/unit, net margin = 30%. Chalice Inc profit = 7 - 4 - 3 - 2 = -2 cents/unit (running at a loss). Candidate should note Cup Co has a healthy 30% margin, while Chalice is losing money on each unit. Candidate should also recognize that if Cup Co matches Chalice's price of 7 cents, its margin falls to zero (10 - 4 - 3 = 3, but price drop of 3 = 0 profit), eroding all profitability.

math.setup: Cup Co: Revenue per unit - Manufacturing - Shipping = Profit. Chalice Inc: Revenue per unit - Manufacturing - Shipping - Distribution = Profit.
steps: Cup Co profit per unit = 10 - 4 - 3 = 3 cents
Chalice Inc profit per unit = 7 - 4 - 3 - 2 = -2 cents
If Cup Co matches price of 7 cents: 7 - 4 - 3 = 0 cents profit (all margin eroded)
math.answer: Cup Co earns 3 cents/unit (30% margin); Chalice Inc loses 2 cents/unit. Price-matching Chalice would destroy Cup Co's margin entirely.

questions.prompt: Why might Chalice Inc be willing to sell below cost in the US market?
questions.guidance: Good candidates brainstorm strategic reasons: (1) Penetration pricing to gain market share; (2) Building US market knowledge and distribution relationships for future product launches; (3) Subsidized by Chinese government or parent company; (4) Using US losses to capture long-term profitability once competitors exit.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, what does customer preference data tell you about Cup Co's competitive position?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) Service reliability is by far the most important attribute to customers (~60% rank it first); (2) Cup Co scores ~9/10 on service reliability vs. Chalice Inc ~3/10 — a significant advantage; (3) Design is the least important attribute; Chalice barely edges Cup Co. (4) Good candidates note that importing from China inherently creates logistics complexity that hurts Chalice's reliability. Implication: price is NOT the primary pain point for customers; Cup Co's core advantage (reliability) is strong.

brainstorming.prompt: Cup Co is currently in a good position relative to Chalice Inc. What are possible strategies to reinforce this position?

categories.name: Offensive Strategies
ideas: Lower prices slightly to send a pricing signal to customers without fully matching Chalice
Negotiate long-term contracts with key restaurant chain customers to lock them in
Explore design improvements (lower priority given customer preference data, but worth considering)

categories.name: Defensive Strategies
ideas: Further improve service reliability — optimize delivery routes to widen the reliability gap
Invest in supply chain resilience to maintain delivery consistency
Highlight reliability track record in customer communications to reinforce switching costs

recommendation: Cup Co should NOT lower its price to match Chalice Inc — doing so would eliminate its entire margin
Cup Co should defend and potentially improve its already high service reliability rating, which is the attribute customers value most
Cup Co can leverage its reliability advantage as a key differentiator and consider locking in customers through long-term contracts
risks: Price may become a bigger pain point if the economy experiences a downturn and restaurant customers face margin pressure
Chalice Inc could improve its logistics and service reliability over time, narrowing Cup Co's key advantage
Other Chinese competitors could enter, increasing downward pressure on price
next_steps: Explore concrete ways to improve service reliability further, such as delivery route optimization
Evaluate feasibility and terms of long-term supply contracts with top restaurant chain customers
Monitor Chalice Inc's pricing and service reliability trajectory over the next 6-12 months
